ambiguities: No unresolved ambiguity in the target's mathematical statement. Natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero; real subtraction is ordinary subtraction.

The algorithm is an exact real-valued recurrence with prescribed multiplicative perturbations. No floating-point format, rounding rule, probabilistic model, overflow restriction, or underflow restriction is specified.

The factor inequality minimizes the quantity Σ_i(factors(i)−1) subject to the stated product constraint. The target does not define algorithms for nonconstant factors or assert that the constant-factor algorithm minimizes actual numerical error.

binders: Universally quantify t,b∈ℕ, then assume 0<t and 0<b. All four conjoined conclusions are under these assumptions.
In the first conclusion only, universally quantify factors:Fin t→ℕ; its positivity and product hypotheses depend on this factors function.
In the fourth conclusion only, universally quantify u∈ℝ, x:Fin(b^t)→ℝ, and δ:ℕ→ℕ→ℕ→ℝ. These may depend on t and b, but this clause is not scoped under the first clause's factors binder.
The fourth clause's perturbation hypothesis universally quantifies level,node,step∈ℕ with the conditional bounds specified below.
conclusions: For every factors:Fin t→ℕ such that factors(i)>0 for every i and ∏_{i=0}^{t−1}factors(i)=b^t, one has t(b−1)≤Σ_{i=0}^{t−1}(factors(i)−1), as an inequality in ℕ.
The product of t copies of b equals b^t: ∏_{i=0}^{t−1}b=b^t.
The sum of t copies of b−1 equals t(b−1): Σ_{i=0}^{t−1}(b−1)=t(b−1), in ℕ.

For every u,x,δ satisfying the fourth clause's hypotheses, |T(t,0)−Σ_{i=0}^{b^t−1}x(i)|≤γ_{t(b−1)}(u)·Σ_{i=0}^{b^t−1}|x(i)|. The right-hand sum is the ℓ¹ norm of the finite real input; the left side is scalar absolute error.
hypotheses: The shared hypotheses are t>0 and b>0.
The first clause assumes each factor is a positive natural number and that their product is exactly b^t.
The fourth clause assumes u>0 and ((t(b−1)):ℝ)u<1, with t(b−1) computed in ℕ before casting to ℝ.
The fourth clause also assumes: for every level,node,step∈ℕ, if level<t, node<b^((t−level)−1), and step<b−1, then |δ(level,node,step)|≤u.
There is no sign, nonzero, or magnitude hypothesis on x. There is no independence or randomness hypothesis on δ, and no constraint on δ outside the stated active ranges.
mathematical_definitions: Write Fin n={0,…,n−1}, N=b^t, and m=t(b−1)∈ℕ. Every natural-number subtraction is truncated at zero; the positivity hypotheses make b−1 and factors(i)−1 ordinary nonnegative differences.
For u∈ℝ and q∈ℕ, define γ_q(u)=((q:ℝ)u)/(1−(q:ℝ)u). Under the error clause's hypotheses, 1−(m:ℝ)u>0.
Extend the finite input to z:ℕ→ℝ by z(n)=x(⟨n,n<N⟩) if n<N and z(n)=0 otherwise.
Given δ, level ℓ, node n, and child sequence c:ℕ→ℝ, define A_{δ,ℓ,n,c}(0)=c(0) and A_{δ,ℓ,n,c}(k+1)=(A_{δ,ℓ,n,c}(k)+c(k+1))(1+δ(ℓ,n,k)) for all k∈ℕ.
Define T(0,n)=z(n). For every ℓ,n∈ℕ, set c_{ℓ,n}(j)=T(ℓ,nb+j) and T(ℓ+1,n)=A_{δ,ℓ,n,c_{ℓ,n}}(b−1). Evaluate the final output at level t and node 0.

For b≥1, each node combines its b children from left to right. The first child initializes the accumulator without a perturbation; each subsequent addition is multiplied by 1+δ at its own step. The perturbation level ℓ labels the construction of T(ℓ+1,n) from level ℓ.
The quantity m=t(b−1) is the error-bound parameter and a maximum number of perturbed additions along an input-to-root path. It is not the total number of additions across the tree.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every positive natural depth t and positive natural branching factor b, four statements hold together. Any t positive natural factors whose product is b^t have total cost Σ_i(factors(i)−1) at least t(b−1). Taking every factor equal to b has exactly the required product and exactly that cost. Moreover, for any positive real u, any b^t real inputs, and any real perturbation array, if t(b−1)u<1 and every perturbation used by the specified regular b-ary tree algorithm has absolute value at most u, then the algorithm's absolute error in summing the inputs is at most [t(b−1)u/(1−t(b−1)u)] times the sum of their absolute values. Each internal node uses the explicitly defined left-to-right perturbed accumulator.

vacuity_risks: For t=0 or b=0, the outer implication is vacuous because a required positivity hypothesis fails. These values are outside the substantive assertion.

The first clause is conditional for each factors function, so it says nothing about a function failing positivity or the product constraint. Its admissible class is nonempty: the constant function factors(i)=b satisfies both.

When b=1, there are no active steps because step<b−1 means step<0. The perturbation hypothesis is then vacuous, m=0, N=1, and the algorithm returns the sole input exactly. The bound has both sides zero, and every u>0 satisfies mu<1.
When b>1, m>0 and the fourth clause requires 0<u<1/m. Such u exist, and δ identically zero satisfies the perturbation hypothesis, so the clause is not vacuous through inconsistent assumptions.
For x identically zero, the algorithm and exact sum are both zero, so the error estimate is trivially satisfied.

Perturbations at unused indices are unconstrained. For the root evaluation with b>0, all accessed perturbations lie in the bounded active ranges and all accessed leaves lie below b^t; the unconstrained values and zero-extension tail do not weaken the stated root bound.
Although the error-constant definition uses total division, the target's strict smallness hypothesis excludes a zero denominator. No substantive case of the asserted bound relies on division by zero.
